text:
incident-bot: ALERT — Dedicated pool 'cynosure-enterprise-prod' GPU utilization 98%, queue depth rising, latency breach detected. Paging on-call.

maria (oncall): on it, pulling metrics now.

maria (oncall): dashboards show sustained 3x traffic from tenant Cynosure for the last 12m, queueing at the front-end, tail latency -> 1.8s for generation calls.

raj (infra): likely a burst from internal batch jobs? Any new rollouts for that tenant?

alyssa (acct-mgr): Cynosure reports timeouts in their customer logs — they're seeing 502s on the production integration. They're pinging us.

kevin-sre: checking autoscaler and pool config. running: `rbctl pool describe cynosure-enterprise-prod`

```
rbctl pool describe cynosure-enterprise-prod
  state: active
  gpus_allocated: 8
  gpus_in_use: 8
  queued_requests: 742
  avg_latency_1m: 1200ms
  burst_policy: preauth_limit=4gpus, auto_burst=false
```

maria (oncall): autoscaler didn't trigger — auto_burst=false for this pool (enterprise policy). Need explicit approval to burst into shared capacity or add reserved GPUs.

raj (infra): we can either 1) approve a cross-tenant burst (+4 GPUs) into shared burst capacity, or 2) enable quick add of reserved GPUs from our capacity pool (slower, ~25m). Which route?

alyssa (acct-mgr): Cynosure has preauth for emergency bursts up to 4 GPUs if we notify them. I messaged their SRE on Slack and emailed PM. Waiting confirmation but they said "ok to proceed" in the thread 2m ago.

maria (oncall): given customer consent, recommend immediate burst +4 GPUs. That will reduce queue and tail latency quickly. Need approval from SRE lead to execute.

kevin-sre: I approve emergency burst per policy. I'll run the burst command and monitor.

kevin-sre: executing: `rbctl pool burst --pool cynosure-enterprise-prod --add-gpus 4 --reason "prod surge, customer consented" --expires-in 60m`

ops-bot: ACTION_LOG: user=kevin-sre action=pool_burst pool=cynosure-enterprise-prod add_gpus=4 expires_in=3600s id=burst-9c4f

incident-bot: NOTE — notify billing and account team for potential overage: ticket auto-generated (#INC-2024-6789).

raj (infra): metrics updating — queued_requests -> 210 within 90s, avg_latency_1m -> 420ms. GPUs in use now 9 (hot rebalancing moving workloads).

maria (oncall): good signal, still watching for noisy clients. Alyssa, confirm with Cynosure they see recovery?

alyssa (acct-mgr): Cynosure SRE: "latency dropping, errors clearing, thanks — hold as long as needed." They asked for an ETA when we can return capacity.

maria (oncall): plan: keep burst for 60m, monitor QPS and queue. If load normalizes, expire burst at +60m. If still high, we'll coordinate infra to extend and get formal billing sign-off.

kevin-sre: creating short incident note: INCIDENT-2024-6789 — Dedicated pool GPU exhaustion for Cynosure; approved emergency burst +4 GPUs; queued requests decreased; burst expires at 60m unless extended.

ops-bot: INCIDENT_LOG: id=INCIDENT-2024-6789 status=investigating owner=maria oncall impact=customer-visible

maria (oncall): retrospective notes to add: tune pre-scaling for this tenant, consider enabling auto_burst with threshold and whitelist for Cynosure (they opted into emergency bursts). I'll open a follow-up ticket for infra + product to review burst policy for VPC/dedicated pools.

alyssa (acct-mgr): I'll follow up with billing and the customer to document approval and cost. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

kevin-sre: closing loop here, will post final status once the burst expires and metrics stabilize.

incident-bot: RESOLVED? waiting for final confirmation from owner."
